What is the Amphitheater of El Jem known for?
The 3rd largest Roman amphitheater in the world, built in 238 AD.
What is the Capitol of Dougga dedicated to?
Dedicated to the Capitoline Triad: Jupiter, Juno, and Minerva.
What are the Antonine Baths known for?
The largest thermal baths built by the Romans on African soil.
What is the Zaghouan Aqueduct?
A 130km structure built by Hadrian to supply water to Carthage.
What is unique about the Temples of Sbeitla?
Features three separate temples instead of one shared Capitol.
Why were the Underground Villas built?
Built underground to stay cool during the summer heat.
What is notable about the Uthina Amphitheater?
A massive site partially hollowed out from a natural hillside.
What is the Arch of Trajan?
A triumphal arch standing at the entrance of ancient Mactaris.
What did the Giallo Antico Quarries produce?
Produced rare yellow marble prized across the Roman Empire.
What is the Byzantine Fortress known for?
One of the most extensive fortresses in North Africa.
What are the Roman Mausoleums famous for?
Famous for its exceptionally preserved funeral towers.
What does the Market of Sertius showcase?
Showcases sophisticated urban commercial planning in Roman Africa.
What was Thuburbo Majus originally?
A Punic town that became a prosperous Roman colony.
Where is the restored Roman Theater of Carthage located?
Located on the hill of Odeon, it now hosts the International Festival.
What was the main function of Gigthis in Roman times?
A major port city facilitating trade between Rome and Sub-Saharan Africa.
What did the Romans build over the Punic Ports?
They maintained the circular layout but added Roman naval infrastructure.
What is the site of Pupput known for today?
A Roman colony near Hammamet famous for its mosaics and necropolis.
Where is the Carthage National Museum situated?
On the Byrsa Hill, the heart of the ancient city.
